versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10045 at 14 FR 1227 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed March 15, 1949; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the March 18, 1949 issue. Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 2034 to 2876 of the held text, from the enacting words to the last operative sentence; the dossier's two spans begin at the heading and then run on into unrelated page text after the order ends. The order's heading and recitals precede it in the held text and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Wabash Railroad Company and the Ann Arbor Railroad Company, carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, the Order of Railway Conductors and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, labor organizations. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Wabash Railroad Company and the Ann Arbor Railroad Company or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10045 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy for Emergency Board No. 71 (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10045_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10045_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_40f7c1ee3a.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has no board report on the merits; it states that the board stood by until April 4, 1949, when the parties appeared in open session and reported full, complete and final disposition and settlement of all matters in dispute (the National Mediation Board index shows the case closed on April 6, 1949, an index entry and not a report date). The board therefore made no report on the merits; the report deadline and the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C), and the order was functionally spent no later than April 4, 1949, the date the parties reported settlement, a date taken from the board's own record and not a date of any report. It stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering this passage, so it is stated here and not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing, the National Mediation Board report copy and in the printing of Executive Order 10044, on whose Federal Register page this order's heading also appears; none of those texts acts on this order. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order without a saving clause; the order created a board for one dispute and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown, and section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues on its own force. The bounded search covered the held text of Executive Order 12553, the order's own text and the OFR catalog disposition notes.
